day_shape: 73 items dominated by heavy IRIB/Defa Press logistical coverage of the Shahid leader funeral in Tehran, Huckabee Jerusalem Post interview ruling out frozen-fund release, reported US-Iran indirect technical talks in Doha, and Jerusalem Post report of aborted Strait of Hormuz escort mission; nothing from UK Parliament or OFAC.

threads.label: Shahid leader funeral logistics in Tehran
threads.summary: Iranian state and IRGC-affiliated channels detailed preparations for the farewell and funeral ceremony of the 'Shahid leader,' including 420 Mouqab, 1,635 accommodation centres for 700,000+ pilgrims, 24-hour Tehran Metro from Friday, and 50% hotel discounts. Defa Press said the Army deployed all three services, two field hospitals, 100 ambulances and 8,000 utility personnel across Tehran, Mashhad and Qom.

threads.label: US-Iran MOU and Doha talks
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post cited a US official saying no frozen Iranian funds have been or will be released unless Iran meets MOU requirements, while Reuters reported indirect US-Iran technical talks underway in Doha with Qatari and Pakistani mediation. Ambassador Mike Huckabee told the Post the US sees no meaningful shift in Tehran and will not accept claims of pragmatism; IRIB reported Iranian negotiator Gharibaabadi met Qatar's PM and FM.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz escort mission fallout
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported that the US and Saudi Arabia clashed over Operation Project Freedom, forcing the Trump administration to abort its mission to escort vessels through the Strait of Hormuz. Defa Press claimed Germany's Defence Minister Boris Pistorius called off deployment of two navy ships from Djibouti for Strait of Hormuz mine-clearing, and cited a UKMTO warning of a suspicious vessel 85nm south of Balhaf, Yemen.

threads.label: IDF Gaza strikes and named eliminations
threads.summary: The IDF announced the killing of Hamas platoon commander Adel Jihad Mohammad Asfour in southern Gaza and, separately, four Hamas operatives — Wael Mahmoud Ali Labad, Muaz Mohammad Hassan Ahmad, Sameh Abu Kamil and Akram Ashraf Hamad Labad — struck over the past week. The military said it also dismantled rocket-launching tunnel shafts; Smotrich said the IDF should seize more than the 70% of Gaza it currently controls.

threads.label: Israel–Lebanon deal and Hezbollah messaging
threads.summary: Netanyahu told a Second Lebanon War memorial that Lebanon is paying the 'price of the war' due to Hezbollah, while Defense Minister Katz invoked October 7, and President Herzog told the Romanian Parliament he praised US officials for negotiating the recent Israel-Lebanon deal. IDF Arabic spokesperson Avichay Adraee posted a message attacking Hezbollah's Lebanese identity; a Jerusalem Post opinion framed the US-Israel-Lebanon agreement as a turning point.

threads.label: Iranian threat rhetoric and Israeli measures
threads.summary: Defa Press quoted Foreign Minister Araghchi warning that 'any threat against our nation and leadership will be met with an immediate and powerful response,' referring to the Islamabad memorandum, while Khamenei's office reiterated continued support for 'resistance against the Zionist-American enemy.' Netanyahu told Channel 14 a third Iran confrontation is possible 'if necessary'; Israeli Defense Minister Katz sanctioned 37 cryptocurrency wallets linked to the IRGC.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressures
threads.summary: Iran International reported insulin costs in Iran rising more than 24-fold in under two months for one NovoMix FlexPen patient as insurance lags, and said state broadcaster IRIB cut short a Ghalibaf interview, prompting parliamentary protests over suspected censorship. The Jerusalem Post reported Iran has threatened to confiscate Tehran's Saint Peter Evangelical (Qavam) Church compound and evict 20 resident families.

Two weeks earlier, a draft of this plan, which 'Itamar Ben-Gvir', the Zionist regime's Minister of Internal Security, was one of the proposers of, was approved. Behind the figures of casualties lies the story of the lives of thousands of civilians, including journalists, health workers and rescue forces who, according to international law, enjoy special protection. Widespread destruction of homes, infrastructure, places of worship and cultural heritage in southern Lebanon has had profound effects on the lives of civilians.

Mechanic Certification: Inspection Rating and Recent Experience Requirements
events.summary: FAA proposes to amend the regulations for certificated mechanics by replacing the inspection authorization with an inspection rating on a mechanic's certificate, similar to the existing airframe and powerplant ratings. The inspection rating would carry the same privileges and limitations as the inspection authorization but would not require renewal or have an expiration date, consistent with the other mechanic ratings. As a result, FAA proposes to require certificated mechanics with inspection ratings to complete rolling recent experience activities, maintained independently, to exercise the privileges of their rating, rather than the current requirements of presenting evidence of renewal activities each March of every odd- numbered year. These proposed changes are intended to align mechanic privileges, which would streamline and simplify the process for maintaining inspection privileges, increase FAA efficiency by reducing on-demand work tasks, and save critical hours for safety-focused missions. These proposed changes would be deregulatory since they would reduce the paperwork and resource burdens linked to complying with the existing regulations for both industry and FAA.
